subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and fix ACPX/Claude launch readiness, or intentionally introduce a concurrency gate for ACP spawns?
rationale: Current tests and docs protect distinct ACP sessions running in parallel, so a serialization-style workaround is a behavior decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and fix launch readiness
options.body: Keep distinct ACP child sessions concurrent and require live proof to isolate the ACPX/Claude startup failure before changing OpenClaw orchestration.

options.title: Add an explicit ACP concurrency gate
options.body: Intentionally serialize or cap ACP spawns beyond the existing `maxConcurrentSessions` behavior, accepting the product tradeoff for reliability.

options.title: Close after live non-repro
options.body: Run the current two-spawn smoke on latest ACPX/Claude and close only if both children reliably launch and emit output.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and fix launch readiness
recommendation.body: Keep distinct ACP child sessions concurrent and require live proof to isolate the ACPX/Claude startup failure before changing OpenClaw orchestration.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the ACP thread-bound agents control-plane and spawn behavior that defines the current concurrency contract.
